messages.content: You are a creative storyteller. Write vivid prose with strong imagery.
Write a 200-word short story about a lighthouse keeper who finds a message in a bottle from herself.

message.content:
The sea threw it against the rocks just after midnight, the way it always did — dragging things from somewhere dark and delivering them to her doorstep. Maren pulled the cork with two fingers, careful not to tear the paper inside.

*You will stop lighting the lamp on March 3rd.*

She read it once. Twice. The handwriting was hers — she would have sworn on it — the same crooked *a*, the same heavy slant of the *t*. But she had never written this. She checked the date. March 3rd. Tomorrow.

For hours she paced the spiral stairs, the lighthouse groaning around her like a living thing. Who else could have known the exact color of her ink, the way she pressed so hard the nib left grooves in the page?

At dawn she climbed to the lamp and lit it anyway. She would not be a woman who obeyed warnings written by strangers, even strangers wearing her hand.

The sea was quiet that day. No ships came.

On March 4th, walking the tide line, she found another bottle. Same paper. Same ink.

*You will stop lighting the lamp on March 5th.*

Maren sat down in the wet sand and laughed until the gulls scattered, because she understood now that she had always been the storm, and the storm had always been coming, and she had been sending herself home for years.
